TRACE

180minutes
48solder joints
difficulty

A two-channel phone oscilloscope with a protected input

Heat the pad and the pin together for two seconds. Feed solder into the joint, not onto the iron. Take the solder away first, then the iron.

Strip 3 mm, twist the strands, and tin the end before you solder it to a pad.

Unplug USB and disconnect any battery before you solder or change a wire. Work on a surface that does not burn, and wash your hands after handling solder.

17TRACE-WIRE-1

Before you switch it on

  1. Look. Every joint is a shiny cone. No solder touches a neighbouring pad. No stray strands of wire.
  2. These must not beep. Set the multimeter to continuity and probe each pair. A beep means a short: find it before you plug in.
    3V3GND
  3. These must beep. Probe the two ends of every connection.
    3V3Pico W 3V3 · MCP6002 8 · C1 100n 2 · RXa 270k 2 · RXb 270k 2
    GNDPico W AGND · MCP6002 4 · C1 100n 1 · R2a 390k 2 · BNC1 GND · BNC2 GND · R2b 390k 2
    CH1_INBNC1 SIG · R1a 820k 1
    CH1_NODER1a 820k 2 · R2a 390k 1 · RXa 270k 1 · MCP6002 3
    CH1_BUFMCP6002 1 · ROa 100R 1 · MCP6002 2
    SCOPE_CH1ROa 100R 2 · Pico W GP26
    CH2_INBNC2 SIG · R1b 820k 1
    CH2_NODER1b 820k 2 · R2b 390k 1 · RXb 270k 1 · MCP6002 5
    CH2_BUFMCP6002 7 · ROb 100R 1 · MCP6002 6
    SCOPE_CH2ROb 100R 2 · Pico W GP27
  4. Plug in. Nothing gets warm, nothing smells. If something does, unplug at once and go back to step 2.
  5. Flash the bring-up test. It reports every part it can find before you load the real firmware.pio run -e bringup -t upload && pio device monitor
18TRACE-WIRE-1

Trace is built

Trace turns a Raspberry Pi Pico W and an Android phone into a two-channel, 500 kS/s oscilloscope for low-voltage hobby circuits. A small analog front end divides and offsets each BNC input so about -10 to +10 V lands inside the Pico's 0 to 3.3 V ADC, through a buffer that can never drive the ADC past its rails. It runs the upstream Scoppy firmware and app, over a USB OTG cable or Wi-Fi.
